prompt: What really caused the 2008 financial crisis? Tell it as a story starting from the US housing boom, include subprime mortgages, securitization, Lehman Brothers and the government response.

plan.title: What Really Caused the 2008 Financial Crisis
plan.description: The 2008 financial crisis grew from the US housing boom, subprime mortgages and securitization. It peaked with the fall of Lehman Brothers and a sweeping government response.

beats.narration: A housing boom nearly broke the world economy. Banks handed out subprime mortgages, loans to borrowers unlikely to repay, because house prices only seemed to rise.

props.text: Cheap loans. Rising prices. Nobody worried.

beats.narration: Then banks bundled those loans into securities and sold them worldwide. Risk spread everywhere, and almost nobody knew who held the bad debt.
When prices fell, borrowers defaulted and those securities collapsed. In September 2008, Lehman Brothers went bankrupt, and panic froze lending across the globe.
Governments answered with bailouts and emergency support to keep banks alive. The lesson: when everyone shares the risk, one failure can topple everything.
